standard.name: General Style and Coding Standards for Software Projects (preliminary version, 2015)
standard.publisher: Standards Group, IT department (author date 2015-03-20; approved 2015-03-26)

assumptions: The document lists type prefixes for Boolean (bl, bln), char, short, long, float, double, bit, byte and string, but its own examples also use 'i' (integer) and 'dt' (date time); both are accepted as prefixes.

The document shows lowercase words after a variable prefix (i_student_total_num) but capitalised words in booleans, functions and in code (bln_Save_Completed, i_Get_Time, i_max_Score, str_Student_Name). Only the prefix and the underscore separation are enforced; capitalisation of the words after the prefix is not.
'bl' and 'bln' are both listed for Boolean; every example uses 'bln'. Both are accepted.

Functions that return a value use kind 'function'; functions with no return value use kind 'procedure' (the document calls them 'function without return type'). A code analyzer knows the return type, so this split is available at retrieval time.
The document says a type name is [noun]_Type. Class, enum and interface names are all treated as types.
The document's own Java figure declares 'calcSqrt', which does not follow its own function rule; the rule text, not the figure, is treated as normative.

Structure rules (else after if, comments before conditionals/loops/external calls, try/catch/finally) are recorded but not evaluated by Athena Sim v0.1; the retrieval index is keyed by identifier kind, so they are only reachable through the full-document and chunk conditions.
The stray bullet 'cxcx' at the end of the document is treated as an editing artefact and dropped.

rules.description: Names of variables should be a noun with or without a modifier and use a prefix to identify the data type of the variable: [type prefix]_[noun], [type prefix]_[adjective] or [type prefix]_[adjective]_[noun]. The prefix is followed by an underscore and the words are separated by underscores. Clear, complete and meaningful names make the code more readable.
rules.rationale: The prefix shows the data type at every use of the variable.

rules.description: The name of a Boolean variable starts with the Boolean type prefix (bln; the type table also lists bl), then a verb and an object or an adjective: [return_type]_[verb]_[noun]_[adjective].
rules.rationale: A Boolean reads like a question or state: bln_Is_File_Opened.

rules.description: Names of constants are nouns in capital letters, with or without modifiers: [adjective]_[noun] (MAX_LINES, PI, AVERAGE_GPA).
rules.rationale: Capital letters make constants recognisable at a glance.

rules.description: A function without a return value (procedure) is named with a verb and, whenever appropriate, an object: [verb]_[object]. The verb starts with a capital letter and words are separated by underscores (Enter_Height_and_Weight, Calculate_GPAX). No type prefix.
rules.rationale: Verb-object names say what the procedure does.
rules.sourceSection: Naming Convention for Functions - function without return type

rules.description: A function that returns a value uses a prefix identifying the return type, then a verb and a noun: [return_type]_[verb]_[noun]. The verb starts with a capital letter and words are separated by underscores (i_Get_Time, bln_Create_OutputFile).
rules.rationale: The prefix shows the return type at every call.
rules.sourceSection: Naming Convention for Functions - function with return type

rules.description: All names of types use the letters Type: [noun]_Type (subject_Type, license_Type, bankAccount_Type).
rules.rationale: Type names are recognisable by their suffix.

rules.description:
Put a comment before starting a function or procedure to describe the objective of the function, its input parameters and its returned value, using this template:
/* Function Objective:
Input parameters :
Function description:
Return Value : [void, int, float, string] GPA value
Created By : Programmer A
Create Date:
Revised By:
Revised Date:
*/
When using IF, always use Else (the else branch carries a comment explaining why the condition failed).
Always put a comment before starting a conditional or loop, and a comment for each call to an external function that explains the input parameters and the returned output.

Use Try..Catch..and Finally as always inside the program. Catch exceptions that exactly match the possible exceptions. All lines of code have to be under a Try..Catch block or within a thrown exception.
